additional_concerns: Candidates node.074087c89e3a3304960f612e, node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 turn preservation of an existing application process into substantive unavailability of relief. The source establishes preserved processing, but does not expressly establish that stronger consequence. This is an unresolved inference, not a demonstrated contradiction.

A historical pending-at-commencement flag remains true after later approval, withdrawal or replacement. The source does not establish a permanent change-level disqualification based on that history. No withdrawal, resubmission or severability rule should be inferred.

The explicit commencement date is supported. The supplied source does not independently reconcile immediate effect with publication timing or specify a universal assessment-versus-implementation event test.

The relevant amended FAQs and any SFC clarification connecting preserved processing to relief availability are missing. The two supplied missing dependency IDs have no identifying descriptions, so neither can safely be matched to those authorities. Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements are also needed to determine factual home compliance, although the formulas expressly accept that classification as an input.

Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question rather than deciding their substantive eligibility. Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa assesses substantive conditions only. Neither answers actual relief availability for a preserved application.

The introduction describes home supervision as the measures' purpose; item (ii) expressly tests home-requirement compliance. A separate home-supervision condition is not established for item (ii). Notification and post-vetting remain distinct from these scoped predicates.
